superseded_pilot.reason: The first failed batch completed coherent ordinary replay but invalidated the submit capture. Attempting another instanced batch therefore failed. The corrected fixture checks invalidation, re-captures its unchanged descriptor only for ordinary drawing of the remainder, and checks all 25 actual successful draws. It does not interpret recovered E_FAIL as success.

limits: Only immutable fixed-fixture resources, two warmed effects and one pass are qualified; arbitrary live sources and full scene/Present are not.

The first shader preparation failure is injected at the real device call. It tests one complete coherent failure branch. It does not prove arbitrary asynchronous driver-error propagation or actual lost-device recovery.
Ordinary fallback re-captures the restored fixture descriptor after API error and disables batching for the remainder of that group. A later group starts a new checked capture.

Five group sizes (1, 2, 15, 16, 25), regular/extra states and actual successful device draw counts are checked before timing. The observer and device/state-block audit wrappers are removed before all timings.

Five-way uninstrumented rotations include native bulk, direct first-batch capture, worker first-batch capture, original per-mesh worker and prior bulk worker. Every pair retains frame ownership/start handoffs and final GPU drain.
Previous Begin(flags=7), deferred driver errors and narrow native bulk-capture predicate limitations remain. These timings provide neither a gameplay FPS estimate nor multiplayer qualification.
Packet lifecycle regressions use the unchanged ordinary-leader default; they do not qualify the new command path for live Reset or teardown.
next_boundary: Measure merging the redundant ownership/frame-start messages while preserving FIFO publication, window-thread ownership and complete GPU timings; then qualify live resource/error/lifecycle boundaries before runtime promotion.
